parts.title: Campus Conversation: Borrowing a Library Book
script: Narrator
Listen to a conversation between a student and a librarian.
Student
Hello. I need a book for my history class, but I can't find it on the shelf.
Librarian
What is the title? I can check the computer.
Student
It's called The Roman Empire, by Helen Brooks.
Librarian
Let me see. Ah, it is checked out. Another student borrowed it last week. It should come back on Friday.
Student
Friday is too late. My paper is due on Thursday. Is there another way to get it?
Librarian
You could read the electronic version. You can open it on your laptop with your student number.
Student
That's great. Can I print some pages from it?
Librarian
Yes, but printing costs ten cents a page. Also, you can reserve the paper copy, and we will send you an email when it arrives.
Student
I'll do both. I'd like the paper copy for my next project.
Librarian
Okay. I just need your name and student number.
Student
Sure. It's Anna Lopez, and my number is four seven two one.
Librarian
Thank you. You will get an email on Friday.
Narrator
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Narrator
Listen again to part of the conversation. Then answer the question.
Student
Friday is too late. My paper is due on Thursday. Is there another way to get it?

questions.q: Why does the student talk to the librarian?
o: She wants to find a book she needs
She wants to pay a late fee
She wants to return a book
She wants a job at the library
questions.exp: She cannot find the history book on the shelf.

questions.q: Why can't the student borrow the book now?
o: It is in the wrong room
questions.exp: The librarian says it is checked out.

questions.q: When is the student's paper due?
questions.exp: She says it is due on Thursday.

questions.q: Why does the student say this: "Is there another way to get it?"
o: She is asking for a different solution
She is complaining about the price
questions.exp: She needs the book sooner, so she asks for another option.

questions.q: What will the student probably do first?
o: Ask her teacher for more time
questions.exp: She says she will do both, and the electronic version is available now.

parts.title: Lecture: How Bees Make Honey
script: Narrator
Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.
Professor
Today we will talk about honeybees and how they make honey. Honey is the food that bees store for the winter, when there are no flowers.
Professor
The process begins with worker bees. A worker bee flies from flower to flower and drinks a sweet liquid called nectar. She keeps the nectar in a special stomach.
Professor
When she returns to the hive, she gives the nectar to another bee. That bee chews it for about half an hour. This chewing adds a chemical that changes the nectar.
Professor
But the nectar is still too watery. So the bees put it into small wax cells and fan it with their wings. The fanning removes the water. After a few days, the liquid becomes thick.
Professor
Finally, the bees cover each cell with wax to keep the honey fresh. Honey can stay good for many years this way.
Professor
It is amazing how much work this takes. One bee makes only about one twelfth of a spoon of honey in her whole life!
Professor
So, to review: first, collect nectar; second, chew it; third, dry it by fanning; and fourth, seal it with wax.
Narrator
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Narrator
Listen again to part of the lecture. Then answer the question.
Professor
It is amazing how much work this takes. One bee makes only about one twelfth of a spoon of honey in her whole life!

questions.q: What is the lecture mainly about?
questions.exp: The professor explains the process of making honey.

questions.q: What do worker bees collect from flowers?
questions.exp: They drink a sweet liquid called nectar.

questions.q: Why do bees fan the nectar with their wings?
questions.exp: Fanning removes the water so the honey becomes thick.

questions.q: Why do bees cover the cells with wax?
Why does the professor say this: "It is amazing how much work this takes"?
o: To show how little honey one bee makes
questions.exp: He stresses the large effort for a tiny amount of honey.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the process?
o: Collect nectar, chew it, fan it, seal it
Seal it, fan it, chew it, collect nectar
Chew it, collect nectar, seal it, fan it
Fan it, collect nectar, seal it, chew it
questions.exp: The professor reviews the four steps at the end.
